hypotheses.justification: Its only use is passing it to abs_eigenvector_of_top_eigenvector. That lemma's proof never uses its corresponding parameter _hT_compact. Inlining that proof without the parameter leaves the remaining proof unchanged, including all degenerate cases.

A direct argument avoids self-adjointness. Set a = |f|, u = a + f and v = a - f, both nonnegative. The eigenvector equation, norm_abs_eq_norm and hlam₀_top give ⟨a,Ta⟩ ≤ ⟨f,Tf⟩. Expanding shows ⟨u,Tv⟩ + ⟨v,Tu⟩ ≤ 0. Both terms are nonnegative by positivity preservation, so ⟨u,Tv⟩ = 0. If v = 0, f is nonnegative. Otherwise Tv is strictly positive almost everywhere; L2.inner_def, L2.integrable_inner and integral_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg_ae imply u = 0 almost everywhere, hence u = 0 by Lp.eq_zero_iff_ae_eq_zero. Thus -f is nonnegative. Apply ground_state_strictly_positive to f or -f respectively. Zero measure is excluded by hf_ne; neither this argument nor the final positivity step needs self-adjointness.

Positivity follows from the other assumptions. Let a = |f|, which is nonnegative and nonzero by norm_abs_eq_norm and hf_ne. Positivity improvement gives Ta > 0 almost everywhere. Consequently ⟨a,Ta⟩ > 0: it is nonnegative, and equality would imply a·Ta = 0 almost everywhere using L2.inner_def, L2.integrable_inner and integral_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg_ae, forcing a = 0 by Lp.eq_zero_iff_ae_eq_zero. Now hlam₀_top gives 0 < ⟨a,Ta⟩ ≤ lam₀ * ‖a‖², forcing lam₀ > 0. Supply this derived fact to the original proof. This also handles degeneracy: zero measure would contradict hf_ne.
